Title: Police widen probe into RM4.83mil drug haul at Subang Air Base
Article:
KUANTAN: Police are working with the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) to identify and arrest more people linked to a drug syndicate that exploited military assets.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 13 people had been arrested so far, comprising seven RMAF officers and personnel and six civilians.
"I believe more arrests will follow as investigations progress, particularly involving those with information about the case.
"Cooperation between the police and the military, especially the RMAF, has been good, with joint operations yielding results," he told reporters at the Pahang police headquarters today.
Khalid said investigations into other potential suspects were ongoing, while remand orders for the 13 detainees had been extended.
Those involved would be charged once investigations were completed, he said.
He was speaking after witnessing the handover of duties between incoming Pahang police chief Datuk Mohammad Shaharul Md Osman and acting state police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob, who is also the deputy state police chief.
The arrests followed the seizure of 96.6kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million at Subang Air Base last week, with operations conducted in the Klang Valley, Labuan and Sabah.
Those detained included an RMAF pilot and two syndicate coordinators. The pilot is believed to have acted as a coordinator and transporter for the syndicate.
Yesterday, Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said
the syndicate
had transported drugs from Subang to Labuan and Tawau, Sabah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US signals tariffs of 18-25pct, Malaysia insists on 19pct ceiling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue negotiations with the United States until the first quarter of 2027, when a final decision on tariffs relating to excess capacity under Section 301 is expected.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the US had indicated a tariff range of between 18 per cent and 25 per cent for Malaysia.
He maintained that Malaysia's overall tariff rate should not exceed the 19 per cent previously agreed upon under the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART).
"From now on, we need to continue engaging with them and putting forward our arguments until the first quarter of next year, when they will make their final decision.
"Whatever it is, our overall tariff as a country must not exceed 19 per cent," he told reporters after an event commemorating BYD's local assembly initiative in Malaysia today.
More to come

Title: 69,000 MSMEs voluntarily adopt e-invoicing despite exemption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Some 69,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of between RM1 million and RM3 million have voluntarily adopted e-invoicing despite being exempted from its mandatory implementation.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said more than 270,000 taxpayers had implemented e-invoicing since its phased introduction in 2024, generating a total of 2.23 billion e-invoices.
Of these, 172,000 taxpayers had voluntarily adopted the system despite not falling under any of the mandatory implementation phases.
"Under Phase 4, the annual sales threshold was raised from RM1 million to RM3 million, as announced by the prime minister on Aug 30, 2026.
"With the increase in the threshold, businesses with annual sales of less than RM3 million are exempted from implementing e-invoicing.
"Nevertheless, 69,000 MSMEs with annual sales of between RM1 million and RM3 million have voluntarily implemented e-invoicing," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam) on the number of businesses that had implemented e-invoicing before the exemption threshold was raised and whether compensation would be provided for compliance costs incurred.
Liew said 5,500 taxpayers had implemented e-invoicing under Phase 1, followed by 14,600 under Phase 2, 51,900 under Phase 3 and 26,000 under Phase 4.
Phase 1 began on Aug 1, 2024, involving businesses with annual sales of RM100 million and above, followed by Phase 2 on Jan 1, 2025, covering businesses with annual sales of between RM25 million and RM100 million.
Phase 3 began on July 1, 2025, covering businesses with annual sales of between RM5 million and RM25 million, while Phase 4 covers businesses with annual sales of between RM3 million and RM5 million.
In a supplementary question, Wee asked why a significant number of MSMEs continued to adopt e-invoicing despite no longer being required to do so.
Liew said e-invoicing could benefit businesses by enabling them to maintain more comprehensive financial records, potentially improving their access to financing.
"What is important is that e-invoicing benefits companies that have implemented the system.
"When they approach banks or financial institutions, they already have more comprehensive records, which can help them secure loans or other forms of financing," he said.
Liew said the government's decision to raise the exemption threshold reflected its willingness to listen to businesses' concerns.
He added that businesses which voluntarily implemented e-invoicing remained eligible for the tax incentives provided by the government.
Responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Awang Solahuddin Hashim (PN-Pendang), Liew reiterated that voluntary adoption of e-invoicing could help businesses maintain more systematic records for their own benefit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More commercial vehicle accidents year-to-date than whole of 2025: APAD
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: The number of accidents involving commercial vehicles in Malaysia year-to-date has been higher than last year.
Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) director general Ahmad Radhi Maarof said commercial vehicles are essential to Malaysia's economic activities as they support factories, businesses, retailers and communities nationwide.
However, he noted that Malaysia is seeing a rise in accidents involving these vehicles. No figures were disclosed.
"When a large commercial vehicle is involved in a serious accident, the consequences can be extensive.
"This is unfortunate to say, but for the whole of last year in 2025c we had around 105 accidents involving commercial vehicles.
"We have yet to complete the whole year but the number of accidents involving commercial vehicles already exceeds last year," he said at Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd's Transport Excellence Day here today.
He said despite the use of technology to instil safety elements in commercial vehicles, the driver remains the central aspect of a journey.
"Safety therefore begins with basic but essential responsibilities," he said, adding that every transport operator should ensure that the vehicle is safe to be used on a daily basis.
As a regulatory body, Radhi said APAD establishes standards and licencing requirements.
Its goal is also to prevent any unwanted incidents from taking place on the road.
"So, basically, the goal here is not simply to respond correctly when something goes wrong.
"The goal should be to prevent it from going wrong in the first place, because that's more important," he added.
For transport operators, he noted that compliance should be treated as a minimum standard, not a final condition.
"The better operators will use data to understand this, invest in drivers, maintain vehicles responsibly, and prepare for an industry in which transparency, digital capability, and environmental performance become increasingly important."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore to confront social media platforms over child sex crimes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will meet its Indonesian and Singaporean counterparts in mid-December to send a strong message to social media platforms over child sexual crimes.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil told the Dewan Rakyat today that the government would not tolerate such crimes being committed through social media platforms.
"Whether these platforms cooperate, we pray for the best," he said.
He said Malaysia would adopt age verification, rather than the age assurance approach used by Australia, to prevent children from communicating with adults who might groom them.
He cited a case in Sabah earlier this year in which a 20-year-old man befriended a 15-year-old girl on TikTok before sexually assaulting her.
"We do not intend to restrict their right to communicate. The problem is that these platforms allow sexual predators to operate and exploit children," he said.
Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had asked service providers to remove 40,214 pieces of bullying content and 55 pieces of offensive content involving children between Jan 1 and Nov 15.
He clarified that the bullying figure covered all age groups and referred to content removed, not the number of cases or victims.
He was responding to Datuk Siti Zailah Mohd Yusoff (PN-Rantau Panjang), who asked about online harm involving children this year and the effectiveness of the social media licensing framework.
Fahmi said MCMC supported police investigations through technical assistance, information sharing, digital forensic analysis and joint operations.
This year, Operation Cyber Guardian 2026 led to 69 arrests and the seizure of 498,690 digital files, including 204,934 files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM).
Op Pedo 3.0, conducted from Sept 14 to 16, involved 52 raids and 53 arrests, including eight teenagers.
Op Pedo 1.0 had earlier resulted in several arrests and the seizure of more than 40,000 similar files.
Op Pedo 2.0, from Sept 22 to 30 last year, saw 37 raids in nine states, 31 arrests and more than 880,000 files seized, and 17 people were later charged.
Fahmi said MCMC had also taken enforcement action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 this year, with 25 cases charged in court, 16 compounded and 41 issued warning letters.
The commission was also monitoring compliance with the Child Protection Code under the Online Safety Act 2025 by licensed service providers, he said.
In response to a supplementary question, Fahmi said the government had no plans to completely bar children from social media or create a dedicated platform for them, stressing that parents had an important role in monitoring their children's online activity.
"Do we know what our children watch on social media? Do we know who they are talking to? If we do not, we should stop, investigate and check, and block access if necessary," he said.
More than
2.1 million files
containing CSAM and pornography have been uncovered through Op Pedo and Operation Cyber Guardian since 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia must build new growth engines, reduce reliance on US demand – Liew
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to strengthen its middle class, develop more mid-sized companies and build greater technological ownership to create new engines of growth amid shifting global economic and geopolitical dynamics.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the country could no longer rely heavily on external demand, particularly from the United States as the consumer of last resort, and must instead build stronger domestic and regional purchasing power.
He said a larger middle class with better-paying jobs, alongside more Malaysian companies with the capabilities to scale up, would help drive economic growth and reduce dependence on individual export markets.
"The world has been dependent on the US market as the consumer of last resort. But it is time for us to really build a strong middle class here.
"When our people are richer, then we are not dependent on one market, not just in Malaysia, but in Asean as well," he said, speaking at the National Economic Outlook Conference 2026 organised by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research today.
Liew outlined several longer-term priorities for Malaysia, including strengthening its position as a middle power, developing its technological capabilities, expanding the care economy and accelerating the transition towards a greener economy.
On technology, he said Malaysia needed to move beyond seeing itself primarily as a trading nation and establish itself as a technology nation by increasing local ownership and capabilities in the sector.
He said greater technological ownership would provide another engine of growth, allowing Malaysian companies to build stronger capabilities and participate more meaningfully in the global technology ecosystem.
Liew also identified the care economy as an important source of employment, particularly as Malaysia moves towards becoming an ageing society.
He said the country needed to ensure that more Malaysians could work in the care sector and receive better wages, and that more people, especially the elderly, had access to adequate care.
The sector would also become increasingly relevant as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes the employment landscape, given that care-related jobs could not be easily replaced by AI, he added.
On sustainability, Liew said climate change could become an engine of economic growth if managed effectively, including through the development of greener and more liveable cities.
He said urban planning should encourage more young people to remain in cities without having to own cars, as Malaysia sought to create more sustainable urban environments.
Beyond domestic priorities, Liew said Malaysia must be more geopolitically literate and position itself as a middle power, given its strategic location amid intensifying competition between major powers.
He said Asean countries, including Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand, should not view one another merely as competitors but take a stronger collective leadership role in deepening regional ties.
The rivalry between the US and China had made Asean increasingly strategic in the global economic landscape, requiring countries in the region to work together to strengthen their position, he said.
This cooperation should also extend to attracting foreign investment, with countries avoiding competition that comes at the expense of labour standards, wages and environmental protections.
Liew said Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam must also ensure that multinational companies paid the taxes they were required to under the Global Minimum Tax, rather than allowing countries to offer special incentives to outbid one another and circumvent the framework.
He said these longer-term priorities required Malaysia to rethink how it approached economic development and identify new ways to sustain growth in an increasingly uncertain global environment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin to brief cabinet on RMAF drug case tomorrow
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will present a full report to the cabinet tomorrow on the drug smuggling case involving Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers.
He said the briefing was important for the government to assess the full implications of the incident, particularly the security of national assets and strategic facilities.
The Home Ministry would focus on lessons from the incident, including the need to tighten security at strategic premises, he said.
"Tomorrow, I believe the Home Ministry will be asked to provide a full report at the cabinet meeting. I also believe the Defence Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin) will do the same.
"Usually, when a serious issue like this arises, the ministers concerned are asked to brief the cabinet," he told a press conference after the Home Ministry's monthly assembly here today.
MORE TO COME

Title: South Korea top court upholds acquittal of ex-president Yoon on perjury charges
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea's top court on Thursday upheld the acquittal of former President Yoon Suk-yeol on perjury charges during the insurrection trial of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, reported Xinhua.
The Supreme Court finalised the acquittal and dismissed an appeal filed by the team of Cho Eun-suk, an independent counsel who led investigations into Yoon's insurrection and other charges.
The special prosecutor team sought a two-year prison sentence in the first trial and a fine of 10 million won (about US$7,460  in the appellate trial.
Yoon was indicted in December 2025 on charges of giving false testimony in the previous month during Han's trial, where the former prime minister faced charges of aiding and abetting the ringleader of the insurrection.
Yoon testified during the hearing that he had already planned to convene a Cabinet meeting and summon additional Cabinet members prior to Han's recommendation on Dec 3, 2024, when Yoon declared the emergency martial law that was revoked by the National Assembly.
The special counsel team, however, argued that Yoon initially had no intention of holding a formal Cabinet meeting, as he summoned only six Cabinet members and later six additional members after receiving Han's advice.

Title: Ministry targets 10-tonne padi yield per hectare by 2030
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry aims to increase average padi yields in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) areas to 10 tonnes per hectare by 2030.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the target, which ranges between seven and 10 tonnes per hectare, would be achieved through modern technology, improved fertilisation and better farming practices.
He said several high-performing plots were already recording yields of between eight and nine tonnes per hectare, with a handful reaching 12 tonnes.
"Before opening new padi fields, which requires time-consuming irrigation and infrastructure development, we must prioritise maximising yields in existing areas," he told reporters today.
He was speaking to reporters after handing over the Kampung Angkat Madani project and agricultural drones under a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative at the Pokok Sena Area Farmers' Organisation office.
Mada recorded a two per cent increase in padi yields this year.
Mohamad said that every additional tonne harvested per hectare could generate about RM500 in extra income for farmers.
On preparations for the northeast monsoon and the El Niño phenomenon, he said the ministry was managing water reserves to ensure sufficient irrigation supplies during prolonged dry spells.
Efforts are underway to increase water storage levels at Kedah's Pedu Dam by taking advantage of current rainfall and limiting water releases, with the aim of ensuring sufficient supplies until at least April next year.
He said the RM245 million valve replacement project at the dam remained on schedule for completion next November to improve structural safety and operational efficiency.
Should water levels fall to a critical point, the ministry would consider cloud seeding based on advice from the Malaysian Meteorological Department to safeguard water supplies for agriculture through April.
Earlier, in his speech, Mohamad said the government had allocated RM500,000 for eight community and infrastructure projects in Kampung Guar Petai under the Kampung Angkat Madani 2026 programme.
He said the projects, completed between June and November, were aimed at bringing development initiatives directly to the community.
They included road upgrades, the installation of solar lamps and home repairs.
The ministry also handed over a licensed fertilising drone under its practical Agricultural TVET programme to help modernise padi farming in the area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt studying age limits, age verification for online gaming platforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying the possibility of imposing age restrictions and verification mechanisms on online gaming platforms to protect children and teenagers.
Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil said there were currently no plans to introduce special licensing requirements for online gaming service providers, similar to those imposed on social media platforms.
However, the government was assessing the risks and appropriate regulatory measures, he said.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) was examining several aspects, including children's safety, user interactions, gaming features and content, as well as safeguards put in place by service providers.
"MCMC is also studying international approaches and practices to identify suitable and effective safeguards.
"Its findings will help determine whether additional safeguards or regulatory measures are needed, including possible age limits and age verification mechanisms for online gaming platforms," he said.
He said the assessment would take into account the Malaysian context, industry developments, identified risks and the effectiveness of existing safeguards.
He was responding to a question from Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor) on whether the government planned to extend social media age restrictions to online gaming platforms, particularly those with a large number of children and teenage users.
Fahmi said the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) had also conducted a public consultation from Sept 9 to Oct 24 to develop a gaming subcode.
He said the process involved a working group comprising various stakeholders, including app store operators, local and international game developers, online safety experts, e-sports industry players, legal practitioners and researchers.
Feedback received would be considered in refining the subcode.
"The government is committed to ensuring that any regulatory measures introduced are evidence-based, proportionate to the level of risk and prioritise the safety of children and teenagers while ensuring the responsible development of the online gaming industry," he said.
In his supplementary question, Lee called for online gaming platforms and social media platforms that posed similar risks to be subjected to similar regulatory treatment.
He cited an incident involving a 6-year-old child in Batu Pahat who was seriously injured in October in an incident linked to Roblox, as well as concerns over extremist recruitment through online gaming platforms.
Fahmi said he supported Lee's view but would defer any decision until the CMCF completed its consultation.
"I support that view, and since CMCF has yet to complete its work in gathering feedback, I am holding off on making any decision on this issue for now," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No compensation for businesses affected by e-invoice exemption change
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will not compensate businesses that incurred e-invoicing compliance costs before the exemption threshold was raised from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual sales.
Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the government had instead introduced tax incentives to ease the compliance burden, including for businesses now exempted from implementing e-invoicing.
"To help businesses reduce the burden of e-invoicing compliance costs, the government does not provide compensation but has introduced tax incentives that can be claimed by all businesses, including those exempted from implementing e-invoicing," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam) on the number of businesses with annual sales of between RM1 million and RM3 million that had implemented e-invoicing before the exemption threshold was raised on Aug 30.
Liew said the incentives included accelerated capital allowance claims for the purchase of information and communications technology (ICT) equipment and computer software packages.
Businesses can claim the full capital allowance within one year for the years of assessment 2026 and 2027, compared with the previous two-year period.
"For example, if a company spends RM10,000 on computers and accounting software to implement e-invoicing in the year of assessment 2026, it is eligible to claim the entire RM10,000 in capital allowances within that year.
"Allowing the full capital allowance to be claimed at once enables companies to enjoy tax savings earlier and helps improve business cash flow," he said.
Liew said businesses were also eligible for tax deductions of up to RM50,000 annually on e-invoicing consultancy costs for the years of assessment 2024 to 2027.
He said a company that incurred RM5,000 in consultancy fees could deduct the entire amount from its business income, resulting in tax savings of RM750 at an applicable tax rate of 15 per cent.
In a supplementary question, Wee pressed the government on whether special compensation would be provided to businesses already tied to software subscriptions, system maintenance and e-invoicing service provider contracts.
Liew reiterated that businesses which had implemented e-invoicing remained eligible for the available tax incentives.
He said the government had taken businesses' concerns into account before deciding to raise the exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drug syndicate smuggled 3 tonnes of meth through RMAF facilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A drug syndicate is believed to have smuggled three tonnes of methamphetamine worth RM156 million through Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aviation facilities in Sabah, exploiting two cells operating in Tawau and Labuan.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat today that the syndicate's Tawau cell had carried out seven transactions involving 1.8 tonnes of drugs worth RM93 million.
Its Labuan cell conducted 14 transactions since August 2024, involving another 1.2 tonnes worth RM63 million.
He said the total quantity could supply up to 15 million people.
"Imagine if we had not crippled this activity. The victims would number in the millions," he said.
Saifuddin said the RMAF Provost Marshal Branch arrested 13 people on Nov 17 and 19, comprising five officers, two other-rank personnel and six civilians.
The authorities also seized 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million, while police confiscated three vehicles worth RM172,062.
He said the syndicate's leader had been identified and was expected to be arrested soon.
Saifuddin was replying to Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who asked how drug syndicates had managed to exploit RMAF aviation facilities in Sabah as an international transit route.
Saifuddin said the government viewed the case seriously as it involved an organised crime syndicate exploiting military personnel, facilities, assets and strategic national infrastructure.
"This is not merely a serious criminal matter. It could also undermine the integrity of our security and defence institutions," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, with the government also looking to invoke organised crime laws, including the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012.
Investigators are identifying the roles of those involved, including financiers, planners, transporters and runners.
Preliminary findings showed that individuals with access to, or links with, military aviation personnel and operations had enabled the syndicate to use the facilities.
Police began gathering intelligence in January 2026 and shared it with the armed forces in September and October.
Saifuddin said the RMAF made the initial detection and arrests on Nov 17 as the area was under its control, before handing the case to police.
He said the operation had been running for several years and involved a large, established syndicate, with some members already charged and jailed.
The trade was highly lucrative, with methamphetamine fetching about RM50,000 per kg locally, RM250,000 in Indonesia and RM450,000 on the international market.
"I assure you that whoever we arrest in the coming days will not escape, regardless of their position or standing," he said.
He added that preliminary briefings had identified several potential suspects who held prominent positions in society.
On Nov 19, police said they were tracking down a Malaysian believed to be the syndicate's
mastermind
following the arrest of five RMAF officers and six civilians in the Klang Valley and Labuan on Nov 17.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SpaceX cleared to launch up to one million AI satellites
Article:
WASHINGTON: SpaceX has received approval to launch up to one million satellites into Earth orbit to establish space-based data centres for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.
The United States (US) Federal Communications Commission (FCC) announced on Wednesday that it had authorised the company's project, dubbed 'Starmind.'
"By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centres are meeting the moment," FCC chairman Brendan Carr said.
Supporters of space-based data centres argue that they could benefit from abundant solar energy and opportunities for cooling in space.
The approval paves the way for a concept that billionaire Elon Musk, who owns SpaceX, made a central part of his presentation during the company's initial public offering.
However, building data centres in space poses significant technical challenges, including the need for large solar panels to generate electricity, sophisticated cooling systems, and technology capable of transmitting vast amounts of data back to Earth.
Under the FCC's approval, SpaceX must deploy 10 per cent of the maximum authorised number of satellites by November 2035.
That figure must rise to 50 per cent by November 2038.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tesla driver pleads guilty to dangerous driving causing woman's death
Article:
KULIM: A factory engineer pleaded guilty at the magistrate's court here today to a charge of dangerous driving that caused the death of a woman on Nov 23.
N. Dinendran, 29, entered the plea after the charge was read before magistrate Nur Hamizah Mat Shah.
The prosecution, however, sought a postponement of sentencing pending the full post-mortem and chemical analysis reports. It also initially proposed bail of RM10,000.
According to the charge, Dinendran drove an electric car, a Tesla, dangerously, causing the death of Noor Lela Zainon, 39.
The offence was allegedly committed at the traffic lights junction near Schott Factory, Taman Teknologi Tinggi Kulim, at 11.50pm on Nov 23.
He was charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for a jail term of between five and 10 years and a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000 upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Ain Fadilla Mohamad Fauzi prosecuted, while Dinendran was represented by National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK) lawyer V Nyanasegaran.
The defence sought a bail reduction, citing the accused's monthly income of RM4,000 and his remorse over the incident.
The court granted bail of RM5,000 with one local surety.
It also ordered Dinendran's driving licence to be suspended pending the disposal of the case and his passport to be surrendered to the court.
The case was fixed for mention on Jan 11, 2027, for the submission of relevant documents, including the post-mortem report.
Earlier, it was reported that Noor Lela, a factory worker, was killed when the Proton Saga she was driving was hit by an electric vehicle believed to have run a
red light
at Jalan KHTP 1, near the Schott Factory junction, on the night of Nov 23.
She died at the scene from severe head injuries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia strengthens access to climate financing despite COP31 pact deadlock
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, has helped strengthen its access to international climate financing despite participating countries failing to reach an agreement on the Antalya Pact.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia had also benefited from exploring green investment opportunities and expanding strategic international cooperation during the conference.
He said the Malaysian delegation had actively participated in climate financing negotiations based on the country's position, which was agreed upon by the National Climate Change Action Council in July and endorsed by the Cabinet in August.
Among the key outcomes agreed upon by participating countries was the implementation of the Climate Finance Work Programme for 2027 and 2028 to operationalise Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement, which requires developed countries to provide financial resources to developing nations.
"Another outcome was the formal discussions on Article 2.1(c) in the context of Article 9 of the Paris Agreement to ensure financial flows are aligned with climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts.
"The negotiations also emphasised the use of grant-based and highly concessional financing through the Green Climate Fund, as well as simplifying funding approval and disbursement procedures through the Global Environment Facility.
"They also focused on strengthening financing to address climate change-related loss and damage through the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage.
"These developments are important in strengthening Malaysia's access to international climate financing," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Muhammad Islahuddin Abas (PN-Mersing) on Malaysia's achievements at COP31, particularly in climate financing, green investment and international cooperation.
Arthur said his ministry, as the national focal point for the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), had coordinated Malaysia's participation, including formal negotiations, the establishment of the Malaysia Pavilion and bilateral meetings.
He said he had also held bilateral meetings with ministers from Fiji, New Zealand and Singapore on the sidelines of COP31 to strengthen international cooperation.
"Although the Antalya Pact was not agreed upon by member countries, negotiations on other agenda items made progress, which will benefit Malaysia.
"Malaysia has successfully safeguarded its national interests and will continue to support the international climate change agenda through climate action and fulfilment of its obligations under the Paris Agreement," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Locking out tomorrow's quantum hackers
Article:
LETTERS:
Imagine a thief attempting to steal a locked safe today, knowing full well he cannot open it yet, simply because of the wait for a master key currently being built in a laboratory.
That scenario is already unfolding across global networks, and it affects everything from your bank balance to your hospital records.
For decades, our online privacy has rested on clever number puzzles that ordinary computers would take millions of years to untangle. Quantum computers, powered by the bizarre rules of subatomic particles, will slice through those puzzles like a hot knife through butter.
Even more alarming is a tactic known as "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later", where shadowy groups siphon off scrambled Internet traffic today to unlock once quantum machines arrive. Anything meant to stay confidential for 10 or 20 years — such as financial histories or state secrets — is already in their crosshairs.
To counter this, Malaysia is championing two vital shields: data sovereignty and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
Data sovereignty keeps Malaysian information housed inside local data centres under domestic jurisdiction, while PQC replaces vulnerable digital padlocks with quantum-proof mathematics.
Fortunately, Putrajaya has moved swiftly while other countries are still debating. Parliament recently heard that Malaysia stands alone in Asean as a Tier 1 nation in the Asean Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness 2026 assessment.
Rather than issuing polite suggestions, authorities are enforcing strict readiness under the Cyber Security Act 2024 and the National Cyber Security Agency's MyKriptografi roadmap.
Inside a dedicated national testing sandbox, cryptographers at the Malaysia Cryptology Technology and Management Centre and CyberSecurity Malaysia are already battle-testing next-generation defences.
At the same time, regulators at the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission are pushing mobile telcos toward quantum-safe networks as scam losses hit RM19.7 billion over the past year.
In an era where an artificial intelligence system recently broke an experimental encryption formula in under three days, building systems that can swap algorithms overnight — known as crypto-agility — has become essential.
Ordinary citizens also face immediate, low-tech cousins of these signal attacks, such as crooks driving around with portable "Fake BTS" transmitters to beam bogus banking alerts onto nearby phones.
Switching off outdated 2G connections in your phone's network settings immediately slams the door on those rogue towers.
Security in the digital age has never been a one-off purchase, much like changing a house lock after losing a spare key.
By reinforcing our national cyber defences today, Malaysia is ensuring that tomorrow's technological leaps do not become yesterday's data breaches.
DR HOE-HAN GOH,
Associate Professor,Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia

Title: Malaysia rules out immediate end to fossil fuel use
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains committed to progressively transitioning away from fossil fuels but will not adopt an approach that calls for their immediate phase-out.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the transition must be fair, gradual, orderly and responsible, taking into account each country's circumstances, capabilities and level of development.
"At the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), I reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to progressively transitioning away from fossil fuels.
"However, Malaysia does not adopt an approach of immediately ending the use of all fossil fuels.
"Nevertheless, Malaysia remains committed to achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Muhammad Islahuddin Abas (PN-Mersing) on Malaysia's position regarding international calls to end the use of fossil fuels, particularly coal, oil and gas.
Islahuddin also asked how the government would ensure a fair and orderly energy transition without compromising energy security, economic growth and the people's well-being.
Arthur said the government was implementing several strategic measures under the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), including gradually phasing out coal-fired power generation.
He said Malaysia would not develop new coal-fired power plants, while existing facilities would cease operations in stages upon the expiry of their respective power purchase agreements (PPAs).
"With this, the last coal-fired power plant is scheduled to cease operations in 2044.
"We will also retain the role of natural gas as a transition fuel to ensure the stability and security of the country's electricity supply," he said.
Arthur said the government would also expand renewable energy development and battery energy storage systems (BESS), alongside modernising the country's grid infrastructure.
These measures are aimed at achieving the country's target of 70 per cent renewable energy installed capacity by 2050.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Snooker centre caretaker pleads guilty to exposing daughter to injury
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A snooker centre caretaker whose one-year-old daughter died after suffering multiple injuries pleaded guilty at the Sessions Court today to exposing the child to physical injury at a motel earlier this month.
Siti Aishah Ali, 25, who is of Thai descent, broke down in tears when she entered the plea before judge Juraidah Abbas.
A woman believed to be her relative, who was seated in the public gallery, also wept. After the proceedings, the woman hugged Siti Aishah, and both cried uncontrollably.
According to the charge sheet, Siti Aishah, who is the caregiver of her year-old daughter, allegedly exposed the child in a manner likely to cause her to suffer injuries to her head and abdomen.
The child died a day after being admitted to Penang Hospital, where medical examinations revealed injuries to her abdomen, legs, forehead and back.
The offence was allegedly committed at a motel on Lebuh Penang between 8.19am on Nov 16 and 2.29am on Nov 18.
The charge was framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Yap Tsu Sheng prosecuted while Siti Aishah was unrepresented.
Yap told the court that she had pleaded guilty without legal representation and requested a date for the submission of documents and appointment of a lawyer.
He opposed bail, citing her Thai citizenship, lack of identification documents, absence of a permanent address and risk of flight.
Juraidah denied bail and fixed Dec 28 for the submission of documents and appointment of a lawyer.
It was reported recently that Siti Aishah and her boyfriend had been remanded over the alleged abuse of her one-year-old daughter.
The pair were
arrested
on Nov 17 at Penang Hospital after bringing the child in for treatment for vomiting and ill health.
Medical examinations revealed that the infant had sustained injuries to her abdomen, legs, forehead and back, raising suspicions of physical abuse.
The child died a day after being admitted to the hospital.
The child's remains have since been handed over to her grandmother for burial.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia faces hurdles in enforcing transboundary haze laws
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Enforcing laws against transboundary haze pollution faces challenges, particularly when those responsible operate outside Malaysia's jurisdiction.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said any proposal for new legislation must be assessed for its effectiveness, enforceability, evidential requirements, diplomatic implications and compatibility with existing laws.
He said proving that haze originated from a neighbouring country would require sufficient evidence, including location maps, coordinates, landownership details and information on parties operating at fire sites.
"This also involves issues of information confidentiality, security and the sovereignty of the country where the haze originates," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) had asked whether the government would reconsider its earlier decision and enact a specific law on transboundary haze pollution, including mechanisms to hold Malaysian individuals or companies accountable if their overseas operations were proven to contribute to haze affecting the country.
Arthur said the government took transboundary haze incidents seriously and was continually reviewing measures, including the feasibility of enacting a Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
He said the ministry had examined the proposal from various angles, including legal feasibility, diplomatic relations with regional neighbours and similar legislation in other countries.
"The effectiveness of a law depends not merely on its provisions, but also on the ability to obtain evidence, conduct investigations and enforce it against parties outside Malaysia's jurisdiction," he said.
Arthur said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry and Plantation and Commodities Ministry had examined allegations involving Malaysian companies with ownership, investment or operational links to fires in Indonesia.
"Based on checks so far, there is no strong evidence confirming the involvement of Malaysian-linked plantation companies as the parties causing those fires," he said.
On corporate accountability, he said the Second Asean Haze-Free Roadmap (2023-2030), under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), provided a framework for member states to implement national measures.
He said Strategy 6.5 of the roadmap's Monitoring and Evaluation Framework called on member states to adopt national policies, including the polluter-pays principle, to hold polluters accountable under their respective laws.
Each Asean member state was responsible for implementing its commitments through domestic policies, legislation and enforcement mechanisms, he added.
Arthur said enforcement against parties responsible for fires was therefore subject to the domestic jurisdiction and laws of the country where the fires and haze originated.
On further action, he said the government would use lessons from this year's haze episodes to review and strengthen existing mechanisms.
He said tackling transboundary haze required more than legislation, including stronger enforcement of domestic laws against open burning, better information sharing and closer cross-border cooperation.
"Malaysia will raise this matter at the upcoming transboundary haze meeting under the AATHP," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EPF manages RM1.55 trillion in assets as of September: Finance Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) had RM1.55 trillion in investment assets as at Sept 30, according to the Finance Ministry.
The EPF's dividend payouts depend on market conditions and its ability to generate sustainable long-term returns.
In a written parliamentary reply, the ministry said EPF aims to generate competitive real returns on members' retirement savings over the long term, across different market cycles.
It said short-term market movements and the broader economic environment play an important role in determining the dividend rates declared by the retirement fund.
To sustain competitive dividend payouts, the EPF adopts a disciplined investment strategy based on Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA), spreading investments across different asset classes, sectors, geographical markets and investment mandates.
The allocation is guided by risk tolerance limits approved by the EPF board, allowing the fund to balance return objectives against investment risks.
The ministry said the EPF was also strengthening its organisational capabilities through human capital development, greater use of technology and data, and stronger governance practices.
These measures are aimed at supporting the effective execution of its investment strategy and risk management framework, in line with its long-term objectives and prudent investment principles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retirement funding – how do we prepare for an aged society? [WATCH]
Article:
Malaysia is already an ageing nation, and is expected to become an aged nation – when 14 per cent or more of the population are made up of those of 65 years and older – by 2048.
Rising healthcare and pension costs, a shrinking ratio of working-age adults to older persons, retirement income adequacy, and greater need for elder care and senior-friendly transport and housing are some of the challenges that we as a nation will be facing in just about two decades.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir announced that a White Paper on Malaysia's preparations to become an aged nation is expected to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat on December 2, outlining whole-of-society planning.
How should we prepare for becoming an aged nation? Are our retirement funding system at an optimal level, and if not, how do we boost our funding system to ensure that we are prepared for the challenges and opportunities that come with a Silver Economy?
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen cashier shoved, kicked after customer complains about colleague's expression
Article:
MELAKA: A 17-year-old cashier was shoved and kicked by members of a family after a customer complained about the facial expression of her colleague at a mini-market in Taman Bertam Perdana.
Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said initial investigations found that the incident occurred at 9.30pm on Sunday when a female customer approached the payment counter to buy a packet of cigarettes.
He said the woman took issue with the victim's colleague, who was manning the counter, and told her to smile, saying she was annoyed by her facial expression.
The woman then left the shop, but her husband arrived shortly afterwards, accompanied by their four children.
"The man threw a cigarette box at the victim before shouting, 'Who threw cigarettes at my wife?'
"He then approached the victim and shoved her forcefully towards a refrigerator.
"A woman believed to be his daughter also entered the shop, shouted at the victim and kicked her several times on the legs," he said when contacted.
Halim said the man's wife later returned to the shop and calmed the situation before the family left in a dark blue vehicle.
The victim lodged a police report and sought treatment at a hospital, he said.
"The case is being investigated under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation, which carries a jail term of up to two years, a fine or both, and Section 323 for voluntarily causing hurt, punishable with up to one year's imprisonment, a fine of up to RM2,000 or both.
"Police are tracking down everyone involved in the incident," he said.
Earlier, a one-minute-and-20-second video of the incident went viral on social media after it was shared by a user claiming to be the victim's older sister, who called for police action against those involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelana Jaya Line resumes normal operations after repairs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Train services on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal following the completion of repair works after a power supply disruption affected four stations.
RapidKL said in a statement on its official WhatsApp channel that repairs at Subang Jaya, Glenmarie, Ara Damansara and Lembah Subang stations had been completed.
Alternative train and bus services deployed during the disruption have also been discontinued.
However, train frequencies are still being adjusted following the restoration of services.
Passengers were advised to check service updates and plan their journeys accordingly.
Earlier, the disruption during the morning peak hour
frustrated commuters
travelling to work.
Checks on social media platform Threads found several passengers complaining about delays and partial platform closures at the four affected stations.
Some also called for better operational efficiency and service consistency to prevent further delays and additional transport costs, particularly during peak hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jendela contractor in Sabah hit with over RM200mil in penalties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A company involved in implementing the National Digital Network (Jendela) Phase 1 project in Sabah was penalised more than RM200 million for failing to fulfil its contractual obligations.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the amount was almost equivalent to the value of the contract awarded to the company.
He said penalties imposed under Jendela Phase 1 were calculated based on the number of sites awarded to each company.
"The penalties or fines imposed under Phase 1 were particularly severe for the companies as they were based on the number of sites awarded.
"There were companies that failed to deliver. For example, in Sabah, there was a case where the penalties exceeded RM200 million, which was almost equivalent to the contract value.
"The contract was awarded before my tenure," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Shaharizukirnain Abdul Kadir (PN-Setiu) on penalties imposed on contractors who failed to complete telecommunications towers within the stipulated period, as well as measures to prevent similar problems under Jendela Phase 2.
Fahmi said the ministry had tightened subcontracting requirements under Phase 2 following problems involving multiple layers of subcontracting, which resulted in subcontractors not receiving payment.
He said companies awarded Jendela contracts must now notify and obtain approval from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) before subcontracting any work.
"We found that companies awarded contracts would subcontract the work through multiple layers, thinking that doing so would make things easier, but the problem was that subcontractors were not paid.
"We have informed all companies awarded contracts that if they intend to subcontract the work, MCMC must be notified and its approval obtained.
"Otherwise, we will not allow the arrangement to proceed," he said.
Fahmi said Jendela Phase 1 had been completed, while the first batch of Phase 2, involving the development of 1,000 sites nationwide, was being implemented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nestle rolls out AI safety tech across entire truck fleet
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: Nestle Malaysia Bhd has achieved 100 per cent GPS, artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled dashcam and telematics coverage across its existing transporter fleet in an effort to enhance visibility across its transport operations.
Chief executive officer Juan Aranols said road safety is a matter that the company takes seriously, as it has more than 200 heavy trucks moving its products nationwide daily.
"Our responsibility does not end when our products leave the factory. It extends to protecting our drivers and everyone who shares the road with them," he said in his speech at Nestle Transport Excellence Day 2026 held here today.
Also present at the event was Land Public Transport Agency director general Ahmad Radhi Maarof.
Nestle Malaysia manages around 6,500 trips covering about 900,000 kilometres every month across its primary transportation network in Malaysia and Singapore.
The integrated system provides real-time visibility of vehicle movements and utilises AI in its dashcams to identify potential safety risks, including speeding, sudden breaking, mobile phone use and driver fatigue.
"Technology gives us greater visibility and insight but what matters is how we use it to prevent incidents and continuously raise safety standards.
"These efforts also support the ambitions of Malaysia's National Transport Policy 2019-2030 towards safer, more efficient and sustainable transportation," added Aranols.
Additionally, Nestle has completed 55 journey risk management assessments to identify potential hazards along delivery routes.
These efforts have contributed to zero road-related fatalities and recordable road incidents year-to-date.
Building on efforts to make logistics operations safer and more efficient, Nestle Malaysia is also advancing lower-carbon transportation, reducing transport-related carbon dioxide emissions by about 59 per cent since 2018 from around 141,000 tonnes to 57,000 tonnes year to date.
Nestle Malaysia also raised its average truck utilisation from 82 per cent in 2018 to 91 per cent in 2026 while progressively adopting the use of electric trucks.
By 2027, the company aims to have its electric trucks cover about 144,000 km annually, further supporting the shift towards lower-emission mobility.
Transport Excellence Day 2026 also featured demonstrations of safety and connected-operations technologies, discussions on sustainability and operational standards.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah to get biggest share of Jendela Phase 2 sites
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sabah is set to receive the largest allocation of telecommunications infrastructure sites under the second batch of the National Digital Network (Jendela) Phase 2 project, which could begin next year.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the first batch of Phase 2 involved the development of 1,000 sites nationwide, with allocations distributed almost equally among Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"For the first batch of Jendela Phase 2, there are 1,000 towers and sites nationwide, with about one-third each in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"For the second batch, which may begin next year, the majority will be in Sabah, with the state receiving the largest allocation of sites," he told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Shaharizukirnain Abdul Kadir (PN-Setiu) on the implementation of the Jendela project.
Fahmi said the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), began implementing the first batch of Jendela Phase 2 in stages this month.
He said the project involved developing 1,000 sites nationwide, including 12 in Johor.
He added that priority would be given to populated areas, particularly rural and remote communities that remained without communications coverage.
"The implementation of Jendela Phase 2 is not specifically limited to providing internet access to schools.
"Instead, priority is given to populated areas, particularly rural and remote areas that have yet to receive communications coverage.
"The selection of suitable or fit-for-purpose technology takes into account factors such as population density, geographical terrain and the availability of existing infrastructure," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's data centre boom faces growing revolt from urban residents
Article:
KASHIWA: Until a few years ago, Susumu Goto's house in Kashiwa, northeast of Tokyo, looked out on a grassy field where neighbours played baseball and soccer.
Today, a couple of 31-metre-tall (102-foot) data centres owned by Hong Kong-based asset manager PAG loom in front of it.
At least once a month, tests of backup generators send black fumes into the sky and the smell of burning fuel hangs in the air.
"Every morning when I step outside, my whole view is swallowed up by the buildings," said the retired auto mechanic.
"It feels oppressive. Seeing that day after day takes a real mental toll."
Each building is the size of a large warehouse but as tall as a 10-storey apartment block.
Loose regulation and political stability have made Japan a magnet for data centre investment even as other countries have put administrative brakes on the industry.
But about 60 per cent of data centres are in and around the densely populated Tokyo metropolitan area, home to about 37 million people, and growing opposition from residents has prompted a review of an industry the government is counting on to drive economic growth.
An action plan aimed partly at heading off disputes is due to be finalised by year-end.
Industry group Japan Data Center Council as well as Tokyo and several other local governments have also drawn up best-practice guidelines this year as data centres have crept ever closer to homes.
DISASTER ZONE
In Tokyo's Koto ward, near Tokyo Bay, Ayano Sasaki worries about what will happen once Singapore-based Empyrion Digital finishes its 51-metre data centre, due for completion in 2029.
Her apartment building stands 3.7 metres from the site of the planned facility, where 1.2 million litres (317,000 gallons) of heavy oil — enough to fill three 25-metre pools — will be buried underground.
The area is designated as both flood-prone and among the capital's highest earthquake-risk zones.
"It's incredible that something like this can be built here without any special regulations," said Sasaki, a 37-year-old nurse.
Residents in Koto have filed appeals with Tokyo demanding binding rules on noise, heat, fuel safety and the placement of data centres. The petitions are awaiting deliberation in the metropolitan assembly.
Empyrion referred questions about the data centre to local consulting firm USI Engineering, which said the site was chosen "after reviewing regulatory compliance, infrastructure conditions and environmental impact."
Consultancy JLL expects Japan's data centre market, measured by revenue, to grow to US$33.4 billion by 2030 from US$23.4 billion in 2024, representing average annual growth of 6.7 per cent.
TOO CLOSE FOR COMFORT
On a recent afternoon, six backup generators facing Goto's house fired up for a test run, belching out black smoke and hot air with a jet-engine-like whine.
"I can't stand the noise, so I close the windows or leave the house to escape it," the 76-year-old said, looking out from his second-floor window. 'Exhaust settles on his laundry,' he said, 'and the smell can be overpowering.'
Goto's plea to the city to push the developer to locate the underground fuel tanks towards the middle of the roughly 10-hectare site, farther from homes, went nowhere.
The data centres sit among hundreds of houses, some farmland and a baseball field.
The generators are tested whenever a new tenant moves in, and over the past two months they ran for some 110 hours combined.
Two more data centres are planned, meaning the tests will only multiply.
"As long as this continues, I'll keep fighting to protect our living situation, maybe until the day I die," Goto said.
Asked whether proximity to residential areas was considered when selecting a site, PAG said, "We carefully consider numerous factors... including local environmental and community impact, and we work with city, prefectural and community leaders to understand their views before work commences."
FIGHTING IT IN COURT
In Inzai City, between Tokyo and Narita Airport, Junichi Takeda and fellow residents are going a step further by taking their issue to court.
Britain's Colt Data Centre Services began construction this year on a 32-megawatt facility that will rise directly in front of Takeda's apartment 11 metres away, blocking the view from his spacious balcony.
Takeda and fellow plaintiffs are suing the city and Japan ERI, a government-authorised building inspection and certification company, arguing the project was wrongly permitted as an office rather than a factory or warehouse — a classification that would have barred construction there.
"Japan hasn't established the proper laws," said their lawyer, Satoshi Oikawa.
"That's why you're seeing huge data centres being planned in residential areas or in front of train stations. That's threatening people's lives and their rights. It's a big problem."
Inzai City and Japan ERI declined to comment because the cases are ongoing.
Campaigners say the Inzai case could set a precedent for how — or whether — Japanese courts will police the office-zoning loophole developers have used nationwide.
For now, residents are scrambling to raise awareness among the broader public with a simple warning: your community could be next.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Libyan student posts RM17,000 bail in fatal Jalan Jelatek crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Libyan university student charged with reckless driving resulting in the death of a retired soldier along Jalan Jelatek here has been released on RM17,000 bail with assistance from his country's embassy.
A source close to the investigation confirmed that Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, 32, posted bail yesterday.
"He managed to post bail with assistance from his country's embassy," the source said when contacted today.
Ali, who is pursuing a master's degree at a private university,
pleaded not guilty
before magistrate Amalina Johar yesterday.
He was charged with driving a Proton Saga recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Jelatek, from Wangsa Maju towards Taman Keramat, at 1am on Nov 21, resulting in the death of Mohd Hairezam Omar, 43.
The charge was framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a jail term of between 5 and 10 years and a fine of between RM20,000 and RM50,000 upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry objected to bail, citing the seriousness of the offence and the accused's status as a foreign national.
The prosecution had alternatively proposed bail of RM70,000 with two Malaysian sureties if the court decided to grant bail.
However, the accused's lawyer, K. Ramalingam, sought bail of RM10,000, saying his client was scheduled to sit for examinations next month.
The court granted bail of RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties and ordered the accused to surrender his passport and report to a nearby police station once a month.
His driving licence was also suspended pending the disposal of the case.
The court fixed Jan 28 for mention.
It was reported
that the victim was riding his motorcycle from Taman Keramat towards Setiawangsa when a car driven by the accused allegedly ran a red light and struck him.
Hairezam suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
Alcohol and urine screening tests conducted on the accused returned negative results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Kong home prices ease in October as recovery loses steam
Article:
HONG KONG: Hong Kong private home prices dropped 0.6 per cent in October from a month earlier, reversing a recent period of stability, data from the Rating and Valuation Department showed on Thursday.
The private home price index eased in October, following revised gains of 0.2 per cent in September and 0.1 per cent in August.
The index fell in July, marking its first decline since March 2025 after home prices rose about 13 per cent over the preceding 15 months.
The housing market lost momentum amid a stock market correction and tighter Chinese restrictions on outbound investment.
Prices rose 6.5 per cent in the first 10 months of this year.
Hong Kong's property market, one of the world's least affordable, has been supported by improved sentiment, buoyant equity markets, firm demand from a growing number of mainland Chinese professionals and easing oversupply.
Residential prices in the Asian financial hub posted their first annual increase last year after tumbling nearly 30 per cent from their peak in 2021.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor sees rise in flood evacuees as Perak numbers dip
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres (PPS) rose in Selangor, declined slightly in Perak and remained unchanged in Sabah this morning.
In SELANGOR, the number of evacuees increased to 1,456 from 414 families, compared with 958 from 281 families yesterday.
According to the Social Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, Kuala Langat recorded the highest number, with 801 evacuees at two relief centres — 785 at Sekolah Kebangsaan RTB Bukit Changgang and 16 at Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu.
In Kuala Selangor, 449 evacuees were housed at three centres — 214 at Sekolah Rendah Agama Pasangan, 166 at SK Dato' Maharaja Lela and 69 at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok.
In Sepang, 206 evacuees were sheltering at three centres — 122 at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Dato Ahmad Razali, 51 at Dewan Orang Ramai Dengkil and 33 at Dewan Orang Ramai Taman Gemilang.
In PERAK, the number of evacuees at three relief centres across three districts fell slightly to 209 from 62 families, compared with 211 from 63 families yesterday.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the number at Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung remained at 127 from 37 families.
In Hilir Perak, evacuees at Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan fell to 72 from 21 families, while 10 from four families remained at SK Batu Hampar in Larut, Matang and Selama.
The Drainage and Irrigation Department said Sungai Kurau at the Bukit Merah reservoir in Kerian had reached the danger level of 9.25m, against its normal level of 8.68m.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast thunderstorms across all districts in Perak this afternoon.
In SABAH, the number of evacuees in Sook remained unchanged at 153 from 42 families.
The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee said they were from three flood-affected villages and were sheltering at Dewan Serbaguna SLDB in Kampung Dalit Gana.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Over 40,000 bullying posts wiped from social media as MCMC ramps up crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Social media platforms have removed 40,214 bullying-related content and 55 extremely offensive content involving children following requests by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) between Jan 1 and Nov 15 this year.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the statistics on the removal of bullying-related content covered all age groups and referred to the volume of content taken down, rather than the number of criminal cases or victims involved.
He said efforts to address the issue were being carried out in an integrated manner by the ministry and relevant agencies, in accordance with their respective jurisdictions and legal provisions.
“In combating the online sexual exploitation of children, the MCMC also works with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) by providing technical assistance, supplying information and digital forensic analysis, as well as conducting integrated operations,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Fahmi was replying to a question from Datuk Siti Zailah Mohd Yusoff (PN-Rantau Panjang), who wanted to know the number of cases in 2026 involving cyberbullying, sexual exploitation and harmful content targeting children, as well as the effectiveness of the social media platform licensing framework, which came into force on Jan 1, 2025. — Bernama

Title: One in four jobs, RM14.4b in value: Sabah tourism’s economic clout on display
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — Sabah’s tourism industry generated RM14.4 billion last year, accounting for 12.3 per cent of the state’s economy, an increase of 5.6 per cent from the previous year.
Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the figures, published in the Regional Tourism Satellite Account Sabah 2025 by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), highlighted the industry’s growing importance beyond visitor arrivals, particularly in generating income and employment.
According to the DOSM report, retail trade was the largest contributor to the Gross Value Added of the Tourism Industry (GVATI), accounting for 45.6 per cent, followed by accommodation services and food and beverage services at 30 per cent.
Tourism-related industries employed 415,100 people in 2025, an increase of 7.1 per cent from 387,600 the previous year, meaning that almost one in four employed people in Sabah worked in industries linked to tourism.
Domestic tourism consumption rose 14.2 per cent to RM13.4 billion from RM11.7 billion in 2024.
Inbound tourism expenditure recorded the stronger growth, increasing 20.8 per cent to RM7.5 billion, while domestic tourism expenditure grew 6.8 per cent to RM5.9 billion.
Jafry said the report was produced through a collaboration between his ministry and DOSM to provide more comprehensive data on the state’s tourism sector and support evidence-based policymaking.
He said the findings would help the ministry formulate development strategies, particularly ahead of Visit Sabah 2027.
“The success of the tourism sector should not be measured solely by the number of tourist arrivals, but also by how much income the industry generates, the employment opportunities it creates and the extent to which it improves the well-being of Sabahans,” he said.

Title: From traffic lights to petrol pumps, transmission fault disrupts Sabah’s East Coast
Article:
SANDAKAN, Nov 26 — Sabah Electricity (SE) confirmed that an incident on its electricity transmission system at 6.04am on Thursday caused a power outage affecting the East Coast.
The utility company activated its operations room and deployed technical teams to restore electricity supply in stages across Sandakan, Tawau, and Lahad Datu.
SE apologised for the inconvenience caused to consumers and stated that investigations are underway to determine the exact cause of the disruption, with updates to be provided periodically.
Checks in Sandakan showed several petrol stations congested with vehicles as other outlets were forced to cease operations due to the blackout, while motorists were advised to drive cautiously with several traffic lights out of service.
According to sources, kidney dialysis treatments at the Duchess of Kent Hospital Haemodialysis Unit here proceeded as normal using generator sets, which also continue to power the hospital’s main buildings. — Daily Express

Title: Kelana Jaya LRT services restored after power disruption at four stations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Services along the Kelana Jaya LRT line resumed at 10.09am today after Rapid KL completed repairs to the track power supply, which had disrupted operations at four stations this morning.
Rapid KL said in a statement that alternative train services and free shuttle buses introduced earlier had been withdrawn following the restoration of the power supply.
“All trains are now operating along the entire line as usual, while service frequencies are being gradually adjusted to ensure train movements stabilise and return to schedule,” it said.
The earlier disruption affected services at four stations — Subang Jaya, Glenmarie, Ara Damansara and Lembah Subang — leaving commuters facing longer waiting times.
Rapid KL had deployed shuttle trains at estimated 12-minute intervals and free shuttle buses at intervals of 15 to 20 minutes to help passengers continue their journeys.
Commuters were also advised to use alternative rail routes, including the Ampang/Sri Petaling LRT line and the Kajang and Putrajaya MRT lines.
Rapid KL said its technical and operations teams would continue monitoring the power supply and train services to ensure stability following the repairs.
The rail operator apologised for the inconvenience caused and thanked passengers for their patience and cooperation.

Title: Report: Negeri Sembilan Ruler to meet MB, senior Umno leaders today
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 26 — Negeri Sembilan’s months-long political deadlock could be resolved as early as tomorrow, with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir scheduled to hold separate meetings with Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and senior Umno leaders this afternoon, The Star reported.
Ismail’s political future is expected to feature prominently during his audience with the Ruler at Istana Hinggap in Seremban.
The meeting comes amid unresolved vacancies in the state executive council and concerns over the timely tabling of the state’s 2027 Budget.
Tuanku Muhriz is subsequently expected to meet Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, his deputy Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and other senior party leaders.
The talks follow an agreement among 24 of the state’s 25 Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen to leave the choice of menteri besar to their political leadership.
The Star, citing an unnamed source, reported that the uncertainty surrounding Ismail’s position could be settled by Friday.
Central to the leadership dispute is whether Ismail commands majority support in the 36-seat state legislative assembly, a requirement that the palace reiterated last week.
Following an audience with Tuanku Muhriz on November 20, Ismail told reporters that the Ruler had decreed that he continue serving as menteri besar.
However, later that evening, BN and PN assemblymen reached a consensus to abide by their leadership’s decision on resolving the political impasse. Ismail did not attend the meeting.
BN has already put forward a candidate for the state’s top political post, with Ahmad Zahid emphasising that any resolution must respect constitutional requirements and royal authority.

Title: One missing MyKad, one month behind bars: Sabah man’s roti canai run goes horribly wrong
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 26 — A man who went out to buy roti canai without carrying his MyKad ended up spending a month in prison for an immigration offence before being released Wednesday after he was confirmed to be a Malaysian.
Azlanshah Mahathir, 24, was freed by the High Court after Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos set aside his conviction and five-month jail sentence.
He was sentenced by the Sessions Court on Oct 20, this year after pleading guilty to entering Malaysia without a valid entry pass issued under Section 10 of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
However, his citizenship was subsequently confirmed by the National Registration Department (NRD) following biometric fingerprint verification.
Azlanshah, who works as a cargo handler, said he accepted what had happened and would take it as a lesson in life.
He promised to carry his MyKad wherever he would go from now on. — Daily Express

Title: Planning to climb Mount Kinabalu? Sabah to launch new route from Kiau to Marai-Parai on Jan 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — A new Mount Kinabalu climbing route from Kiau to Marai-Parai will be launched on January 16, marking a significant milestone in the development of mountain tourism from the Kadamaian side.
Kadamaian Assemblyman Datuk Ewon Benedick said the first phase of the new climbing route would become one of Sabah’s latest tourism attractions in conjunction with Visit Sabah 2027, while opening up greater economic opportunities for local communities.
He expressed confidence that the development of Mount Kinabalu’s tourism potential from Kadamaian would be a game changer for the local economy.
“I am confident that the development of Mount Kinabalu from the Kadamaian side will be a game changer for the economic activities of the people in Kadamaian,” he said.
Ewon said this following a working visit to the Sabah Parks headquarters here, where he was briefed by its Director Datuk Dr Maklarin Lakim on the implementation and development of tourism initiatives involving Mount Kinabalu from the Kadamaian side.
Apart from the new climbing route from Kiau, Ewon welcomed Sabah Parks’ initiatives to develop Sayap Peak and the tourism potential of Minitinduk George and Mount Nungkok, as well as proposed developments in Melangkap.
He said the development of mountain tourism from Kadamaian was among the main priorities outlined under the Kadamaian Development Master Plan 2020-2035.
These initiatives would be complemented by infrastructure development, including ongoing and upcoming Rural Road Projects (JALB).
Ewon also pledged to support Sabah Parks’ efforts by facilitating the necessary development allocations.
“I will play my role as Kadamaian Assemblyman to complement the efforts of Sabah Parks, particularly in securing the necessary development allocations,” he said.
Also participating in the working visit were representatives from the Sabah State Economic Planning Unit (Upen) and the Visit Sabah 2027 Secretariat. — Daily Express

Title: PAC urges further cuts to subsidised cooking oil quota, warns oversupply risks fuelling smuggling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today urged Putrajaya to further reduce the monthly subsidised cooking oil quota to match actual domestic consumption, warning that excess supply leaves the RM12.138 billion programme vulnerable to smuggling and leakages.
The bipartisan panel recommended that the monthly quota be capped at between 19,000 and 30,000 metric tonnes to align with consumption data.
The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MOF) had previously lowered the monthly quota ceiling from 60,000 to 55,000 metric tonnes in June.
