“The PAC is of the view that this quota must continue to be assessed periodically based on actual transaction data from the eCOSS system so that it aligns with estimated actual domestic demand, which is lower — between 19,000 and 30,000 metric tonnes per month,” PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin told reporters in Parliament.
“Supply assessments are important to prevent oversupply that can open doors to leakages and smuggling.”
The follow-up stems from the committee’s original July 16 report (D.R. 27/2026), which examined serious enforcement and monitoring failures flagged in the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2025.
KPDN submitted its final follow-up report on October 1 before senior officials from both ministries were summoned to proceedings on October 8.
The committee acknowledged progress by both ministries but said sustained reforms were critical across eight key areas, including digitising targeted subsidies.
The panel also welcomed the ban on non-citizens buying packet cooking oil under the Control of Supplies (Prohibition of Sale and Purchase of Controlled Goods) Regulations 2026 (P.U.A. 104/2026) and the eCOSS mobile app pilot.
However, the committee recommended integrating the system with MyDigital ID or existing assistance platforms such as Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), BUDI RON95 and BUDI Diesel.
“KPDN must table an effectiveness report on the pilot project before any nationwide rollout, particularly to address manual record-keeping leakages in areas with poor internet coverage,” Mas Ermieyati, the Masjid Tanah MP, said.
The ministry was also told to expedite document verification and follow-up cost audits with refineries after a survey showed repackagers’ operating costs had risen by 9.63 per cent to RM2,982 per metric tonne.
The PAC said any claims of cost reductions must be verified before subsidy rates are finalised.
It also urged the ministry not to rely solely on dated assessments such as a 2022 KPMG study, and instead to regularly submit updated economic evaluations and market projections to the Cabinet based on current crude palm oil (CPO) price movements.
Addressing supply chain loopholes, the PAC noted the enforcement of procedures for handling waste and damaged cooking oil since May 1 but urged tighter cross-checking of records among repackagers, wholesalers and retailers to prevent manipulation of spoiled-stock reports.
It also called for stringent legal action against parties diverting subsidised cooking oil into the used cooking oil (UCO) supply chain.
The committee noted KPDN’s decision to withdraw 1,370 metric tonnes of repackager quota from foreign-owned refineries from January 1, 2027, stressing that the transition to local refiners must be managed transparently to maintain stable distribution chains and market supply.

Title: Strong flow, high tides and heavy rain combine to breach Bukit Changgang bund in Kuala Langat
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 26 — Unusually strong water flow from Hulu Langat, combined with high tides and heavy rainfall, has been identified as among the factors contributing to a bund breach at the Bukit Changgang Flood Mitigation Project site in Kuala Langat at about 6am yesterday, resulting in flooding.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) recorded 95 millimetres of rainfall in the area yesterday.
“The incident resulted in floodwaters overflowing into a nearby village, with affected residents relocated to a temporary relief centre (PPS) at Sekolah Kebangsaan RTB Bukit Changgang, which opened yesterday.
“As of 8am today, 783 flood victims from 241 families were housed at the PPS,” he said in a statement today.
Ashrul Riezal added that Selangor JBPM had set up two control posts in the affected area and deployed lorries and boats to assist in evacuating residents, particularly the elderly, persons with disabilities, infants and children.
He said hourly monitoring and patrols had been carried out since yesterday to assess the situation, with water levels dropping slightly this morning compared with last night.
“The DID is undertaking repairs to the breached bund, with the work expected to be completed within 24 hours, depending on weather conditions,” he said, adding that two mobile pumps had also been deployed to help pump out floodwaters, supplementing the existing static pumps.
Ashrul Riezal urged residents to refrain from playing in floodwaters, especially near drains, pits or areas with strong currents, to avoid untoward incidents. — Bernama

Title: Johor targets RM5b in halal investments, 5,000 new companies by 2030, state assembly told
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 26 — Johor has set a target of 5,000 new companies, 4,000 skilled workers and RM5 billion in cumulative investment for the state’s halal industry by 2030, said Johor Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid.
He added that the state also aims to achieve RM18 billion in halal exports and a RM24 billion contribution to its gross domestic product (GDP) within the same period.
“The state government acknowledges that it is still a long way to go.
“With 1,298 new companies secured so far, more effort must be made to achieve the targets,” he said at the Johor legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.
Mohd Fared was responding to a question from Ng Yak Howe (PH-Bentayan) on the number of entrepreneurs in Johor who have successfully obtained halal certification since the introduction of the Johor Halal Development Plan (PKHNJ) 2030.
He said 1,298 new applications for Malaysian halal certification (SPHM) from entrepreneurs and companies in Johor had been approved since the launch of PKHNJ 2030 up to November 11.
Mohd Fared, who is also the Semerah assemblyman, said the figures reflected an encouraging response to the initiative, with applications rising from 133 in 2024 to 561 last year before climbing further to 737 as of November 11 this year.
“This year’s figures represent an increase of more than fivefold compared to 2024, reaching 88 per cent of the annual target of 839 applications.
“A majority of the 441 new companies that applied through the Johor Islamic Religious Department (JAINJ) this year, which is at 342 or 77.6 per cent, are Bumiputera entrepreneurs, compared to only 38 per cent among existing certificate holders.
“This is a positive sign that Bumiputera entrepreneurs are becoming increasingly confident in venturing into the halal industry,” he said.
Mohd Fared noted that Johor currently ranks second in Malaysia, behind only Selangor, with 1,743 active halal certification holders and 4,321 active halal certificates.
“A total of 93 per cent of applications were approved within 30 working days. Our efforts are aimed not only at increasing the numbers but also at simplifying the process,” he said.
As of June 2026, Johor had recorded RM790.91 million in approved halal industry investments across 27 projects, ranking second nationwide, Mohd Fared said.
He added that these included the Paris Baguette Halal Hub in Nusajaya and Ellaziq in Simpang Renggam, while Halmas Park at POIC Tanjung Langsat had realised investments totalling RM2.256 billion, creating 2,342 jobs.

Title: Malaysia cannot rely on US consumers forever, Liew Chin Tong says in call for stronger Asean middle class
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia and other Asean countries must build stronger middle-class populations with greater purchasing power to reduce their dependence on the United States as a consumer market, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said.
He said higher wages and developing companies capable of scaling up would be crucial to sustaining economic growth as global production capacity continued to expand.
“We cannot forever depend on the US as the consumer of the last resort,” he told reporters after delivering his opening address at the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research’s (MIER) National Economic Outlook Conference 2026 today.
“When our people are richer, then we are not dependent on one market. Not just in Malaysia but in Asean as well.
“More Malaysians becoming middle class, more Malaysians getting paid better, more Malaysian companies become mid-size companies with capability and ability to scale.”
Liew’s remarks came a day after the US proposed tariffs of up to 18 per cent on Malaysian goods under Section 301 of its Trade Act, citing concerns over industrial policies and excess manufacturing capacity.
Liew also said Malaysia should move beyond being primarily a trading nation and develop greater ownership of technology rather than simply trading goods and services.
“We do not have to be the top tech. We do not have to compete at the top level.”
Instead, Malaysia should establish itself as an indispensable middle player in the global technology supply chain, particularly as companies diversify production away from China, he said.
“Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam together constitute a very important middle in semiconductor,” he said.
Liew also proposed closer links between the defence and semiconductor industries, stressing the need for practical innovation.
“I was deputy defence minister, and I used to openly say that the defence industry had too many traders and not enough innovators,” he said.
He also called for financial institutions to develop a better understanding of technology businesses.
“Every banker knows how to do financing for development, for housing development, but it’s time for us to have more bankers who understand how to finance and how to assess risk in the technology sector,” he said.
Liew noted that although the electrical and electronics sector accounted for about 40 per cent of Malaysia’s exports, technology stocks remained underrepresented on Bursa Malaysia.
He said Malaysia needed more mid-sized companies with the capacity to develop their own technology and scale up their operations.

Title: ‘He is all I have left’: Sister appeals for clues to UKM student missing for five weeks
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 26 — A woman has expressed her concern for the safety of her younger brother, who is believed to have been missing for about five weeks without any news of his whereabouts.
Thirty-three-year-old Nur Fatihah Mat Daud, of Kampung Sedaka Tengah, Yan, said she only learned of the disappearance of her brother, 22-year-old Muhammad Shafik Hidayat, about three days ago through a message that went viral on the WhatsApp application.
“I received a message informing me that my younger brother had not attended classes at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) for quite some time. The university also contacted me to provide an update regarding his disappearance. However, he has yet to be found.
“The last time I was in touch with him was on Oct 3 when I sent him off to board a bus to Kajang. At the time, he was still replying to my messages as usual… but after that, whenever I tried to contact him, there was no response,” she said when contacted by Bernama today.
She said her younger brother had never told her about having any problems, and she had assumed that he was studying at the university and was doing well.
“After our parents died about four to five years ago, he is all I have because we are the only two siblings. I truly hope that my brother will be found soon and that he is safe.
“I have lodged a police report and the university has also informed me that it has filed a police report. I appeal to anyone who may have information or has seen my brother to come forward and assist, or to immediately contact the nearest police station,” she said.
Earlier, news of the disappearance of a third-year student from UKM’s Faculty of Science Citra went viral on social media, saying that the student had been absent from the university for nearly five weeks, and his whereabouts remain unknown.
The university has attempted to contact the student via telephone, but the calls have gone unanswered, and it has appealed to anyone with information about the student’s whereabouts to contact the university or the police immediately. — Bernama

Title: Penang–Kulim as Silicon Valley, Johor as second economic capital: Deputy minister urges states to drive Malaysia’s growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia must move away from concentrating economic decision-making in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya and give states a bigger role in driving their own growth, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said.
He said the country needed a new approach to economic development, envisaging specialised regional economic centres, with Penang and Kulim serving as technology hubs, Johor becoming the country’s second economic capital and Kuching developing into a national energy hub.
“If we start thinking in this way, we will have a lot more political cohesion at the state and federal level, and we can present a new vision that will actually grow the state,” he said at the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research’s (MIER) National Economic Outlook Conference 2026 today.
Liew said decision-making had been heavily concentrated in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya over the years, partly because of the political structure under the previous administration.
However, states had increasingly sought to assert themselves since 2018, creating an opportunity to rethink how economic development could be distributed across the country.
Referring to Sabah, Liew said the additional RM900 million in federal allocation tabled in Parliament, alongside discussions over the state’s 40 per cent revenue entitlement, represented what he described as a positive step towards greater state empowerment.
He said states should be allowed to build on their own economic strengths rather than depend on decisions made at the federal level.
“Think about Penang and Kulim as our Silicon Valley,” he said, adding that some financial institutions could eventually have employees based in Penang to finance technology businesses.
For Johor, he said the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone could help the state become Malaysia’s second economic capital, drawing comparisons with Melbourne in Australia, Busan in South Korea and Osaka in Japan.
“Think of Johor as the second economic capital,” he said.
He also proposed Kuching as a national energy hub, comparing its potential with Perth in Australia, where mining companies have established their headquarters.
“Think of Kuching in that way, that Kuching can be the energy hub for the nation,” he said.
Liew also highlighted the decline of smaller towns, citing Sultan Nazrin Shah’s book on globalisation and how many towns in Perak had become forgotten places over the past five decades.
He said similar trends could be seen in northern and central Johor, where smaller towns had also been left behind.

Title: Lim Guan Eng questions MACC’s handling of KLSCAH land lease probe, RM2.1b overspending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — DAP national adviser Lim Guan Eng has accused the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) of double standards, contrasting its swift investigation into a land lease controversy involving a ministry led by Hannah Yeoh with what he described as its lack of action over RM2.1 billion in overspending by the ministry headed by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
“Has MACC launched an immediate investigation because one ministry is led by a DAP minister, while the other can be delayed because it is headed by an Umno minister who is also the deputy prime minister?” Lim said in a statement today.
His remarks followed confirmation from Yeoh, the minister in the Prime Minister’s Department responsible for Federal Territories, that her aide had been summoned by MACC to give a statement over the extension of the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall’s (KLSCAH) land lease.
The controversy centres on the reduction of the land premium from approximately RM4.67 million to RM1,000 for a 99-year lease.
Yeoh told Parliament on November 23 that the decision complied with established procedures and governance requirements. She also identified seven organisations that had previously been granted the same nominal premium, arguing that KLSCAH had not received preferential treatment.
Among them were the Malaysian Red Crescent Society, the Badminton Association of Malaysia and the National Council of Women’s Organisations Malaysia.
Lim maintained that there had been no abuse of power in the land lease decision.
By contrast, he said, the Ministry of Finance had issued a statement confirming that the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development had exceeded its approved budget allocation by RM2.1 billion.
Lim added that DAP’s Kampar MP Chong Zhemin had lodged a report with MACC on October 6, addressing what he described as the agency’s initial explanation that an investigation could not be launched without a report.
He called on the commission to explain why it had not shown the same urgency in examining the overspending, while raising the possibility that its investigation into the land lease had been prompted by pressure from Barisan Nasional (BN) or Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders.
“The MACC risks losing public confidence in its ability to discharge its duties professionally and independently if the perception that it applies different standards in its investigations is left unaddressed,” he said.

Title: Picasso among four recovered 1MDB artworks that could go on public display by year-end, National Art Gallery says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A painting attributed to Pablo Picasso is among four artworks recovered in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) financial scandal that could go on public display in Malaysia as early as the end of this year, Berita Harian reported.
The National Art Gallery is preparing a special exhibition featuring works attributed to Picasso, Joan Miró, Maurice Utrillo and Balthus, offering the public a rare opportunity to see artworks recovered through international efforts to trace assets linked to the scandal.
The gallery confirmed that curatorial planning was under way but said no exhibition date had been set, with the authentication and ownership status of the works still to be resolved.
The four paintings were identified as Miró’s Composition (1953), Utrillo’s Maison de rendez-vous, rue Saint-Rustique, Montmartre (1934), Balthus’ Étude pour femme couchée (1948) and Picasso’s L’Écuyère et les clowns (1961).
The gallery told Berita Harian that discussions involving the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, the Ministry of Finance and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), among other agencies, were ongoing.
A meeting on October 21 focused on the ownership status of the recovered artworks and the next steps towards staging the exhibition.
“Among the important processes that must first be completed are authenticating the artworks and determining their actual ownership status before further examination can be carried out by conservation specialists,” the gallery said.
“This process is important to ensure that each artwork can be examined and handled in accordance with established art conservation procedures and standards.”
The gallery said the works had already been valued by international auction houses Christie’s and Sotheby’s in the United States, although it was conducting its own assessments as part of the documentation process.
In April, the four paintings were returned to Malaysia and were being held securely at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
Their recovery forms part of a broader international effort to reclaim assets linked to the misappropriation of billions of dollars from 1MDB, a Malaysian state investment fund at the centre of a global financial scandal.
Efforts are also under way to secure the return of seven other artworks linked to 1MDB and held by Christie’s in the United States, the newspaper reported.
Last December, Berita Harian reported that 12 artworks linked to the scandal, then valued at a combined US$30 million (approximately RM140 million at the time), were intended for public exhibition in Malaysia following their repatriation.
The newspaper also reported that six artworks previously owned by 1MDB case witness Jasmine Loo remained in Christie’s custody and could only be released through a US court order.
According to Berita Harian, Malaysia has so far recovered approximately RM31.2 billion in assets linked to 1MDB, representing nearly 70 per cent of the total assets identified.

Title: Selangor flood evacuees jump by 500 in a day, topping 1,400
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The number of flood evacuees housed at temporary relief centres (PPS) increased in Selangor this morning, while declining in Perak and remaining unchanged in Sabah.
In SELANGOR, the number of flood evacuees rose to 1,456 from 414 families, compared with 958 from 281 families yesterday.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Kuala Langat recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 785 sheltering at the PPS at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) RTB Bukit Changgang and another 16 at Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu.
In Kuala Selangor, 214 evacuees are sheltering at the PPS at Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Pasangan, 166 at SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela and 69 at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok.
In Sepang, 122 evacuees are housed at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Dato Ahmad Razali, 51 at Dewan Orang Ramai Dengkil and 33 at Dewan Orang Ramai Taman Gemilang.
In PERAK, the number of flood evacuees at three PPS across three districts stood at 209 from 62 families this morning, down from 211 from 63 families yesterday.
The State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat reported that the number of evacuees sheltering at Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung remained unchanged at 127 from 37 families.
In Hilir Perak, the number of flood evacuees at Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan fell to 72 from 21 families, while 10 evacuees from four families remained at SK Batu Hampar in Larut, Matang and Selama.
According to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS), the water level of Sungai Kurau at the Bukit Merah reservoir in Kerian reached the danger level, with a reading of 9.25 metres compared with the normal level of 8.68 metres.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast thunderstorms across all districts in Perak this afternoon.
In SABAH, the number of flood evacuees in Sook remained unchanged at 153 from 42 families this morning.
The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) said in a statement that residents from three flood-affected villages were sheltering at Dewan Serbaguna SLDB in Kampung Dalit Gana. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh confirms MACC summoned aide over RM1,000 KLSCAH lease
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that her aide has been summoned by anti-corruption investigators in connection with the renewal of a 99-year land lease for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) at a nominal premium of RM1,000, compared with an earlier estimate of nearly RM4.67 million.
In a Facebook post today, Yeoh said three Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers had visited her office at the Federal Territories Department yesterday.
She said the officers “asked for my assistant to be present at MACC this morning to assist in investigation”.
Her confirmation followed a report by Sin Chew Daily last night that her aide had been summoned to give a statement.
The lease renewal has drawn scrutiny since Yeoh announced on November 14 that the government had approved the nominal premium, substantially below the amount previously estimated.
According to media reports, Yeoh had defended the decision, saying the assembly hall had voluntarily changed the land’s classification to institutional use, restricting its potential for major development.
She also pointed to the institution’s historical significance and financial circumstances, noting that the 103-year-old assembly hall had been gazetted as a heritage building in 2007 and recorded an annual operating deficit of about RM400,000.
Yeoh said the lease renewal was decided by a committee chaired by the chief secretary to the government.
She said seven other organisations in Kuala Lumpur had been granted similar nominal premiums for 99-year leases, including Yayasan Tuanku Bainun, the Malaysian Red Crescent Society and the Badminton Association of Malaysia.

Title: All aboard: Abang Jo wants cruise ships dropping anchor off Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 26 — Sarawak plans to build a cruise ship jetty with immigration and customs facilities at Tanjung Sipang, a headland on the northern tip of the Santubong Peninsula near Damai, about 30km from here.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the jetty would ease entry for cruise passengers and could attract more international visitors to Kuching and nearby destinations, including Damai.
He said the state planned to develop the jetty in waters 16 metres deep near the Santubong National Park, as much of Sungai Santubong was shallow.
“We will also build a road linking the site to Damai, which would cost less than dredging the riverbed, a very expensive undertaking,” he told reporters after launching the Sarawakku Sayang programme here yesterday.
Abang Johari said Royal Caribbean International had sent a team from Singapore to assess whether its cruise ships could call at Kuching before sailing on to destinations such as Bali and Kota Kinabalu.
He said the state also planned to upgrade roads in the area to carry two-way traffic, improving access and supporting the development of the Autonomous Rapid Transit (ART) system.
Earlier, in his speech, Abang Johari said planned projects were expected to change the landscape of Lundu, Samariang and Damai, among other areas.
He said plans for Trombol and its surroundings included modern infrastructure, while a Chinese museum and a gold museum would be built in Bau.
“The Rambungan Bridge is expected to be completed next year, linking Lundu and Kuching,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sabah drug ring suspected of exploiting military facilities linked to RM156m in transactions, Parliament told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A drug syndicate suspected of exploiting military aviation facilities in Sabah is believed to have been operating for years, with police intelligence pointing to previous transactions involving three tonnes of drugs worth RM156 million, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said preliminary investigations pointed to an established criminal network whose suspected mastermind had been identified but remained at large.
Speaking during Minister’s Question Time, Saifuddin said police intelligence indicated that the syndicate’s Tawau cell had carried out seven previous transactions involving 1.8 tonnes of drugs worth RM93 million.
Its Labuan cell, meanwhile, had been linked to 14 transactions since August 2024, involving 1.2 tonnes of drugs valued at RM63 million.
Although police began gathering intelligence in January this year, Saifuddin said preliminary investigations suggested that the syndicate had been operating for several years.
He was responding to a question from Bersatu’s Beluran Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Ronald Kiandee on how drug traffickers could exploit Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aviation facilities in Sabah and what measures the government was taking to prevent organised crime from infiltrating the country’s defence institutions.
Police shared their intelligence with the Air Force in September and October, ahead of operations on November 17 and 19.
Saifuddin said the initial operation and arrests were carried out by the RMAF’s Provost Marshal Branch, as the area concerned was under military jurisdiction, before the case was handed over to police.
The operations led to the arrests of 13 people, including seven RMAF personnel — five officers and two personnel of other ranks — and six civilians.
Authorities seized 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million, while police also seized three vehicles valued at RM172,062.
Saifuddin said preliminary investigations had established the involvement of individuals with access to and connections with military personnel and aviation operations, which investigators believe may have enabled the syndicate to exploit military facilities for drug trafficking.
“This is not merely a serious criminal offence; it could also undermine the integrity of our security and defence institutions,” he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, with Saifuddin saying authorities would also invoke the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) as the investigation widened.
Investigators are seeking to establish the full extent of the network, including the identities and roles of those believed to be involved in financing, planning and transporting the drugs.
Saifuddin said an initial briefing had also identified several individuals who may hold positions of prominence in society and could face further investigation.
“This investigation has the potential to uncover a much wider organised crime network,” he said.
The minister added that action would be taken against those implicated, regardless of their position or standing, and expressed confidence that the syndicate’s suspected leader would soon be apprehended.

Title: Health minister pays tribute to donor families behind 16 transplants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Sixteen organ transplants were successfully carried out nationwide over five days, following four organ donations after brain death.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the historic achievement involved donations at Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia, Hospital Melaka, Hospital Shah Alam and Hospital Sultanah Aminah, Johor Bahru.
He said the donors’ and their families’ sacrifice had given patients in need a second chance at life through eight kidney transplants, three liver transplants, one heart transplant and four corneal transplants.
Hospital Selayang and Hospital Kuala Lumpur each carried out four kidney transplants.
“My highest respects and deepest condolences go to the donors and their families. Your courage in making the most noble decision at a time of grief has given others in need a second chance at life,” he said in a post on X yesterday.
Dzulkefly urged those who have pledged to donate organs to inform their families of their wishes, as the understanding and consent of next of kin are key to fulfilling that trust.
He also expressed his appreciation to all healthcare personnel at the National Transplant Centre (NTC) and the organ transplant teams at the hospitals involved, including surgeons, anaesthesiology teams, transplant coordinators, nurses, pharmacists and support staff, for their dedication.
He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) remains committed to strengthening and expanding organ transplant services nationwide through the establishment of the National Transplant Council, which held its first meeting on Nov 2. — Bernama

Title: Transport Ministry: Malaysia weighing national mental health support programme for pilots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Malaysia is assessing the need for a national pilot assistance programme to support pilots’ mental health and wellbeing, the Transport Ministry has said, following a parliamentary question about the potential professional repercussions of seeking help.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) already operated a peer support programme for its employees, initially involving pilots, with professional support provided through Naluri, a mental health and wellbeing service.
“The programme also emphasises confidentiality, independence and trust as important elements in ensuring the effectiveness of support mechanisms for pilots,” it said.
While Malaysia has yet to establish a nationwide programme, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) has conducted mental health awareness programmes and engaged with several airlines on the mental health and wellbeing of pilots.
The aviation regulator has also issued guidance to the industry emphasising the importance of mental health monitoring, safe working environments and access to support services for employees.
“The government, through CAAM, will continue to assess the need to establish a pilot assistance programme at the national level and examine appropriate frameworks and mechanisms to support its implementation, taking into account industry needs and relevant international practices and standards,” the ministry said.
The reply was in response to Seputeh Member of Parliament Teresa Kok (PH-DAP), who had asked whether the government intended to introduce a confidential and non-punitive assistance programme allowing pilots to seek help for stress, depression, addiction or personal problems without fear of losing their licences or careers.

Title: Putrajaya may hold e-commerce platforms accountable for uncertified goods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The government is examining measures to address the sale of uncertified imported products via e-commerce platforms, including potential action against platforms that fail to ensure compliance with quality standards.
Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said his ministry will collaborate with the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to ensure that products sold online meet established standards.
“Many products brought in from abroad are delivered as individual parcels. Although sold at low prices, these items lack quality certification, this includes electrical goods, which are required to meet safety standards.
“So, I have held discussions with KPDN and relevant parties to explore ways to regulate the operations of e-commerce platforms, while simultaneously continuing to encourage the public to purchase goods online,” he told reporters after the Majlis SIRIM Industry 2026 here yesterday.
Johari said this initiative is crucial for protecting consumers from poor-quality or hazardous products, and for ensuring that local manufacturers, who bear the costs of certification, do not face unfair competition from cheaper imported products.
Meanwhile, in his speech, Johari said products entering the Malaysian market must comply with both Malaysian and international standards, just as domestically produced goods are required to meet stringent regulatory requirements.
“In this respect, Malaysia remains firmly committed to addressing the importation and sale of non-compliant products in our domestic market.
“These products not only expose Malaysian consumers to potentially serious health and safety risks but also undermines the competitiveness of our domestic industries,” he said.
The Majlis SIRIM Industri 2026 witnessed SIRIM QAS International Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of SIRIM Bhd, becoming the first certification body in Malaysia and Southeast Asia to receive accreditation for the AS9110 Quality Management System Requirements for Aviation Maintenance Organisations.
AS9110 is an internationally recognised standard for aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) organisations, addressing critical areas such as airworthiness and fight safety, maintenance planning and execution, inspection and testing, risk management, human factors, traceability and technical data control. — Bernama

Title: Govt finds ‘no strong evidence’ Malaysian-linked plantation firms caused Indonesian fires, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A government review has so far found no strong evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES) has said.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, the ministry said it had worked with the Plantation and Commodities Ministry to examine allegations linking Malaysian companies to the fires through their ownership, investments or operations in Indonesia.
“Based on the review to date, there is no strong evidence confirming the involvement of Malaysian-linked plantation companies as the parties responsible for the fires,” it said.
The government has yet to commit to introducing legislation to hold individuals and companies accountable for overseas operations that contribute to transboundary haze affecting Malaysia.
The ministry said it had examined the merits of introducing a transboundary haze pollution act on several occasions, taking into account enforcement challenges, diplomatic relations and the experience of other countries with similar legislation.
“The effectiveness of a law depends not only on the existence of its provisions, but also on the ability to obtain evidence, conduct investigations and enforce the law against parties outside Malaysia’s jurisdiction,” it said.
Establishing responsibility for fires overseas would require sufficient data, including land ownership records and information about companies operating at fire sites, raising issues of confidentiality, security and national sovereignty.
The ministry pointed to the Second Asean Haze-Free Roadmap (2023–2030), which encourages member states to adopt policies such as the “polluter pays” principle to hold those responsible for pollution accountable under their respective domestic laws.
“Enforcement action against any party responsible for fires is subject to the jurisdiction and domestic laws of the Asean member state where the fires and haze originate,” it said.
The ministry said the immediate priority was to strengthen domestic enforcement against open burning across Asean, improve information sharing and deepen cross-border enforcement cooperation.
The reply was in response to Bakri Member of Parliament Tan Hong Pin (PH-DAP), who had asked whether the government would reconsider introducing legislation to hold Malaysian individuals and companies accountable for transboundary haze caused by their overseas operations.
The ministry did not disclose how many companies had been examined, identify them or provide a timeline for a decision on the proposed legislation.

Title: GPS bets on youth as coalition injects fresh blood into election slate
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 26 — The introduction of 11 new faces in Gabungan Parti Sarawak’s (GPS) candidate line-up for the 13th Sarawak State Election reflects the coalition’s efforts to rejuvenate its leadership and encourage greater participation of young professionals in politics.
GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the inclusion of younger candidates, particularly from Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), was a positive development towards ensuring leadership continuity within the coalition.
“Most of the new faces are from PBB. What makes me even more pleased is that almost all of them are relatively young, in their 40s. Most of them are also professionals, which is a positive development.
“Therefore, we hope that these new faces will win the election as part of our efforts to rejuvenate the party and, at the same time, bring the younger generation into leadership,” he told reporters after officiating the BorneoCraft Global 2.0 Expo and Conference (BCG 2.0) here, yesterday.
GPS yesterday announced its full line-up of 82 candidates for the Dec 12 state election, with new faces accounting for approximately 13.4 per cent of the candidates.
Meanwhile, commenting on the recent resignation of senior leaders from GPS component parties, Abdul Karim said such developments should serve as an opportunity for political parties to evaluate their internal weaknesses and strengthen their organisational maturity.
“My personal view is that it could probably make the party more mature. When you see veteran party members leaving, it should prompt the party to reflect on what is happening internally,” he said.
Abdul Karim said disagreements and dissatisfaction with leadership were not uncommon in party politics but declined to elaborate on internal matters involving the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a GPS component party.
Earlier, five PDP service committees in Paradom, Sungai Bidut, Engkilo, Sungai Sadit and Sungai Empawah announced their collective withdrawal from the party following the resignation of former Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) president Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh from PDP.
The Election Commission (EC) has fixed Saturday (Nov 28) for nomination, Dec 8 for early voting and Dec 12 for polling.
For the latest news on the state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Fatal Johor crash now a murder probe after police uncover suspected cable theft link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A fatal road incident in Johor is now being investigated as murder after police uncovered a suspected cable theft link following the discovery of a video circulating on Facebook.
One man died and another was seriously injured in the incident involving a car and a motorcycle in Taman Nusa Bestari, Iskandar Puteri in Johor.
Iskandar Puteri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said in a statement that police received a report of the incident at 4.30am on Tuesday.
The two local men, aged 22 and 34, sustained severe head and leg injuries and were taken to hospital, where one of them died at 10am yesterday. The deceased was not identified in the statement.
The case was initially investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
However, police subsequently discovered a video of the incident circulating on Facebook, posted by a user under the handle “Azman Mann Terr”.
“Further investigation found elements of cable theft behind the incident,” Radin Ramlan said, adding that Telekom Malaysia Johor Baru had also lodged a police report.
The case is now being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, Section 431A of the same law and Section 235 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Police have not disclosed how the suspected cable theft was connected to the incident.
“We are now tracking the suspects and call upon witnesses or those who have information on the incident to come forward to assist the police with investigation,” Radin Ramlan said.
Anyone with information is urged to contact the Iskandar Puteri police control centre at 07-511 3622 or its hotline at 07-511 4486.

Title: Najib drops final bid to revive RM1.9m suit against ex-AG Tommy Thomas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has withdrawn his final bid to revive a RM1.9 million lawsuit against former attorney general Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, ending a six-year legal battle over Thomas’ decision to prosecute him.
Najib withdrew his application for leave to appeal to the Federal Court today, with his lawyer, Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin, telling the court that his client wanted to “focus on pressing issues”, Free Malaysia Todayreported.
No further explanation was given.
A three-member Federal Court bench chaired by Justice Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah struck out the application after lawyers for both sides confirmed an agreement for Najib to pay RM10,000 in costs.
Najib was present in court, where family members and supporters filled the public gallery.
The former prime minister launched the legal action in 2020, accusing Thomas of misfeasance in public office, malicious process and negligence in exercising his constitutional powers to prosecute in cases involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and the International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC).
He sought RM1.9 million in special damages to cover the cost of hiring an audit team to examine documents and assist in preparing his defence.
The High Court struck out the lawsuit in November 2022, a decision upheld by the Court of Appeal on January 13 this year.
Najib subsequently sought permission in March to take the case to the Federal Court, putting forward three questions of law for its consideration.
In its January ruling, the Court of Appeal found that Najib’s lawsuit had been filed prematurely, as the criminal proceedings in question had yet to begin when he initiated the civil action.
It also held that the tort of malicious process was not recognised under Malaysian law.
However, the appellate court rejected the High Court’s findings that Thomas enjoyed immunity and that his actions were beyond judicial scrutiny.

Title: Sarawak teacher gets 260 years’ jail, 24 strokes for sexually assaulting eight young girls
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 26 — The Sri Aman Sessions Court yesterday sentenced a 35-year-old primary school teacher in Engkilili to a total of 260 years in prison and 24 strokes of the cane for 64 charges involving physical sexual offences against eight girls aged between seven and 12.
Judge Iris Awen Jon convicted the man on his own guilty plea and ordered the sentences to run concurrently.
This means the man will serve an effective prison term of 60 years.
In passing sentence, Iris also imposed a total of 160 strokes of the cane for all the charges.
However, the punishment was limited to a maximum of 24 strokes, as provided under Section 288 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Iris further ordered the man to undergo rehabilitative counselling throughout his detention period, in accordance with Section 26 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act (SOACA) 2017.
He was also ordered to undergo two years of supervision under Section 27 of the same Act upon completing his prison sentence.
Of the 64 charges, 59 were brought under SOACA 2017, comprising 22 charges under Section 14(a), 23 charges under Section 5, and 14 charges under Section 10.
Another four charges were brought under Section 377CA of the Penal Code, while one charge was under Section 377C of the same Code.
According to the facts of the cases, the offences came to light after several parents and the victims themselves lodged police reports following revelations of the man’s sexual misconduct, which took place between 2023 and January 2026.
Investigations found that the offences involving the eight victims occurred at several locations, including the school’s resource centre, classrooms, and teachers’ room.
The man was found to have committed various sexual acts against the victims, including touching their private parts and inserting his fingers and a vibrator into their private parts.
He also pulled their hair and slapped their heads and cheeks, besides threatening the girls to prevent them from disclosing his actions.
One victim also shared that the man had offered various gifts, including a skateboard, a hand-held fan, a watch, and school supplies.
Investigations also revealed that the man had engaged in sexual communication with the victims, including showing pornographic videos to a group of pupils and recording sexual acts at several locations within the school compound.
In addition, forensic examinations of mobile phones, a desktop computer, and several hard drives seized from the man’s residence uncovered photographs and videos suspected to contain child sexual abuse material.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Jonathan Lim Hsi How, while the man was represented by lawyers Boston Ho and Clement Hii. — The Borneo Post

Title: Over 436kg of drugs worth RM34.89m seized in three-month KLIA security sweep, home minister says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A three-month security operation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) uncovered 16 drug smuggling cases involving 436.66kg of drugs worth RM34.89 million, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said the operation, conducted between August 10 and November 13, involved 100 per cent baggage and body screening of targeted flights to 10 destinations.
Authorities screened 4,569 flights involving 21,526 flight crew members, conducted 483,119 pat-down searches of passengers and inspected 711,160 pieces of checked baggage.
“As a result of these inspections, 16 prohibited items were detected and 16 drug smuggling cases involving 436.66kg of drugs worth RM34.89 million were thwarted,” he said.
The operation involved cooperation between the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), aviation security personnel, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan).
Saifuddin said the integration of technology and enforcement operations had improved the efficiency of passenger and goods screening at the country’s entry points.
He was responding to Ampang Member of Parliament Rodziah Ismail (PH-PKR), who had asked about the effectiveness of AKPS, particularly in relation to governance, inter-agency integration and operational efficiency.
The written reply did not specify the types of drugs seized, the number of suspects arrested or whether charges had been filed in connection with the 16 cases.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: 19 officers sacked, eight suspended over ‘counter setting’, ‘flying passport’ syndicates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Nineteen officers have been sacked and eight others suspended from duty over integrity breaches linked to “counter setting” and “flying passport” syndicates, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said disciplinary action had been taken against 27 officers as of November 2026, with the eight suspended officers facing charges in court.
“The government maintains a firm and uncompromising approach towards any breach of integrity through prevention programmes and disciplinary action under the Public Officers (Conduct and Discipline) Regulations 1993,” he said.
The figures were disclosed in a reply outlining the performance of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), which now oversees security controls at 123 active entry points nationwide.
Saifuddin said the agency had consolidated the inspection and enforcement functions of six government agencies, including the Immigration Department and Royal Malaysian Customs Department, under a single chain of command.
The value of seizures rose from RM82.10 million in 2025, the agency’s first year of operations, to RM322.74 million in the first 10 months of 2026, involving 16,357 enforcement cases.
“These achievements demonstrate that the establishment of AKPS is not merely an administrative restructuring, but an institutional reform with significant impact in strengthening border security, facilitating trade and tourism, and protecting national revenue,” he said.
Saifuddin was responding to Ampang Member of Parliament Rodziah Ismail (PH-PKR), who had asked about the agency’s effectiveness, particularly in relation to governance, inter-agency integration and operational efficiency.
The written reply did not identify the officers involved, specify their respective agencies or disclose where the integrity breaches occurred.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Pilots, flight crew to face random drug tests under KLIA security overhaul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Pilots and flight crew will be subject to random drug testing under a Cabinet-approved security overhaul aimed at preventing a recurrence of large-scale drug trafficking through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has said.
In a written parliamentary reply yesterday, Saifuddin said the Cabinet had on August 19 approved a joint proposal by the Home Ministry and Transport Ministry to strengthen security controls and screening at KLIA and other international entry points following several security incidents.
“The government, through the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry, consistently accords the highest priority to security controls at all national entry points, particularly at Kuala Lumpur International Airport,” he said.
“The action plan comprises 17 substantive recommendations formulated around three key security pillars, namely aviation security, national and border security, and physical security and protection.”
The plan will be implemented in three phases spanning more than two years.
Saifuddin said the first phase, covering a period of up to six months, would focus on “addressing gaps in security controls by making optimal use of existing statutory powers, personnel and assets”.
The measures include “tightening e-Vetting procedures for security passes, enforcing random drug testing of pilots and flight crew, periodic rotation of personnel working in restricted zones and increasing the visible presence of police personnel”.
Other proposed measures include the redeployment of narcotics detection dogs and the integration of traveller intelligence through the National Immigration Command Centre (NICC).
Saifuddin said the second phase, covering six to 24 months, would focus on “developing new capabilities and procuring strategic high-technology assets”.
These include high-powered baggage scanners, body scanners and closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) analytics, as well as strengthening police canine units and enhancing specialised workforce training.
Under the third phase, spanning more than 24 months, Saifuddin said the government was committed to “comprehensively modernising and transforming the national security system”.
This would involve replacing baggage and body scanners with new-generation AI-powered equipment at all national entry points and modifying terminal and cargo infrastructure according to risk levels.
The long-term measures would also include “reinforcing the NICC as a national intelligence centre and expanding uniform and integrated security control standards across all air, land and sea entry points nationwide”, he said.
Saifuddin was responding to Bersatu’s Ketereh MP Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor, who had asked what proactive measures the ministry was taking to prevent a recurrence of large-scale drug trafficking through KLIA.
The reply did not specify whether random drug testing of pilots and flight crew had already begun.
